text: The effect ultimately that we've seen from a human capital point of view is displacement. We have more people now than we've ever had, but the nature of the work that they do is more strategic.
speaker: Jonathan Becker
context: Lenny asks Jonathan about how AI is impacting the performance marketing industry. Jonathan explains that AI has been influencing their industry for over a decade, as platforms like Google and Facebook have used AI to automate many manual tasks. He describes how this automation has changed the nature of work at his agency, shifting employees from manual implementation work to more strategic responsibilities.
text_ko: 결국 인적 자본(human capital) 관점에서 본 효과는 일자리 대체(displacement)이에요. 지금은 그 어느 때보다도 사람이 많아졌지만, 대신 그들이 하는 일의 성격은 훨씬 더 전략적이에요.
text_zh: 说到底，从人力资本(human capital)的角度看，发生的是岗位置换。我们现在的人比以往任何时候都多，但他们做的工作更多是战略性的。
text_es: Al final, desde la perspectiva del talento humano, lo que hemos visto es una reorientación: ahora tenemos más gente que nunca, pero el trabajo que hacen es mucho más estratégico.
key_sentence: The effect ultimately that we've seen from a human capital point of view is displacement.
original_text: The effect ultimately that we've seen from a human capital point of view is displacement. We have more people now than we've ever had, but the nature of the work that they do is more strategic. It's more about modeling, validation, asking the right questions, being focused around creative levers. And less so the like trench work of implementation and bid modifiers at the keyword level on Google search, and some of the really hardcore manual analysis we had to do.

vocabulary.definition: Human capital refers to the economic value of an individual's skills, knowledge, and experience, which contribute to their productivity and potential in the workforce.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, human capital is a critical asset that organizations invest in through training and development to enhance employee performance and drive innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a focus on the qualitative aspects of the workforce, emphasizing the importance of investing in people as a means to achieve competitive advantage.

vocabulary.definition: Displacement refers to the process of individuals being forced to leave their jobs or roles due to changes in the market, technology, or organizational restructuring.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, displacement often arises from automation, outsourcing, or shifts in consumer demand, necessitating workforce retraining or redeployment.
vocabulary.nuance: While displacement can have negative connotations, it can also imply a transformation towards more efficient or strategic roles within an organization.

vocabulary.definition: Strategic refers to actions or decisions that are carefully planned to achieve long-term objectives and maximize resources effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, strategic planning involves setting goals and determining the best course of action to achieve competitive advantage and ensure sustainability.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of foresight and intentionality, distinguishing between routine operations and those that require a higher level of planning and analysis.

text: On our creative group, we can come up with mockups, in literally, 1% of the time that it took.
speaker: Jonathan Becker
context: Jonathan continues explaining how AI tools are transforming creative work at his performance marketing agency. He describes how AI image generators like Dall-E and MidJourney allow his creative team to produce initial mockups and concept artwork dramatically faster than before. However, he emphasizes that human expertise is still needed to ask the right questions and iterate on the AI-generated outputs.
text_ko: 우리 크리에이티브팀은 말 그대로 예전에 걸리던 시간의 1%만에 목업(mockup)을 만들어낼 수 있어요.
text_zh: 我们创意团队现在做一个效果图（mockups），真的只要以前用时的1%。
text_es: En nuestro equipo creativo hacemos maquetas (mockups) en apenas el 1% del tiempo que antes nos llevaba.
key_sentence: we can come up with mockups, in literally, 1% of the time that it took.
original_text: On our creative group, we can come up with mockups, in literally, 1% of the time that it took. And so you still have to understand what questions to ask of the AI and be capable of iterating, but these rough drafts that you might show the artwork of to a client to say, 'Do we like this more or do we like this more?' That's AI generated. It's really interesting.

vocabulary.definition: A visual representation or prototype of a product, often used to demonstrate design concepts before final production.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and design industries, mockups are crucial for visualizing ideas, gathering feedback, and making iterative improvements before launching a product.
vocabulary.nuance: Mockups can range from low-fidelity sketches to high-fidelity digital designs; the term should be used to clarify the level of detail in the representation.

text: I always say to people that the first rule of performance marketing is not to forget about offline marketing and the classic marketing that works for organizations. In other words, direct mail can really work, email marketing works beautifully, SEO can really work.
speaker: Jonathan Becker
context: Lenny asks about the perception that paid growth can become addictive like a drug for companies. Jonathan addresses this concern by explaining his philosophy of marketing channel diversification. He warns against putting all marketing budget into a single performance marketing channel, comparing it to investing all your money in one stock. He emphasizes the importance of maintaining a mix of both online and offline marketing channels to avoid volatility.
text_ko: 저는 늘 퍼포먼스 마케팅(performance marketing)에서 가장 중요한 규칙 하나는 오프라인 마케팅(offline marketing)과 조직에서 통하는 전통적 마케팅을 잊지 않는 것이라고 말해요. 즉, 다이렉트 메일(direct mail)은 의외로 효과가 있고, 이메일 마케팅(email marketing)은 정말 잘 먹혀요. 검색엔진 최적화(SEO)도 충분히 성과를 낼 수 있어요.
text_zh: 我总跟人说，做绩效营销（performance marketing）的第一条原则就是别忘了线下营销（offline marketing）和那些对公司真的管用的传统营销。换句话说，直邮（direct mail）确实能奏效，邮件营销（email marketing）效果也很好，搜索引擎优化（SEO）同样有效。
text_es: Siempre digo que la primera regla del marketing de resultados (performance marketing) es no olvidar el marketing offline ni el marketing clásico que funciona para las empresas. Es decir, el correo directo (direct mail) puede funcionar de verdad, el marketing por correo electrónico (email marketing) funciona de maravilla y la optimización para motores de búsqueda (SEO) también puede dar resultados.
key_sentence: the first rule of performance marketing is not to forget about offline marketing and the classic marketing that works for organizations.
original_text: I always say to people that the first rule of performance marketing is not to forget about offline marketing and the classic marketing that works for organizations. In other words, direct mail can really work, email marketing works beautifully, SEO can really work. There's all of these wonderful things at your disposal. The real crash and burn scenarios that I've seen are these, not fly by night brands, but brands that figured out... Just like with Uber, I figured out this weird tie-in where I could make free money from their referral system.

vocabulary.definition: Performance marketing refers to online marketing strategies that are focused on measurable results, where advertisers pay only for specific actions taken by consumers, such as clicks or conversions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, performance marketing is often used to optimize advertising budgets by ensuring that spending is directly tied to measurable outcomes, making it a popular choice for digital campaigns.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes accountability and efficiency in marketing efforts, and is best used when discussing data-driven strategies rather than traditional advertising methods.

vocabulary.definition: Offline marketing encompasses traditional marketing methods that do not involve the internet, such as print advertisements, television commercials, and direct mail campaigns.
vocabulary.businessContext: Businesses often integrate offline marketing strategies to reach audiences that may not be active online, ensuring a comprehensive approach to brand visibility and customer engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: While often considered less measurable than online methods, offline marketing can evoke a sense of trust and familiarity, making it valuable in certain contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Direct mail is a form of advertising that involves sending physical promotional materials, such as postcards or catalogs, directly to potential customers' mailboxes.
vocabulary.businessContext: Businesses use direct mail to target specific demographics with personalized messages, often resulting in higher response rates compared to digital campaigns.
vocabulary.nuance: While often seen as outdated in the digital age, direct mail can be highly effective for certain audiences and industries, particularly when combined with digital efforts.

text: Sometimes people find shortcuts, hacks if you will, to scale rapidly because of one specific nuance of the Facebook ad platform, or something like that. And what they fail to see is that those loopholes come and go.
speaker: Jonathan Becker
context: Jonathan continues his explanation about why over-reliance on performance marketing can be dangerous. He describes how some companies discover temporary advantages or 'loopholes' in advertising platforms that allow them to scale quickly and cheaply. However, he warns that these advantages are typically short-lived, and companies that build their entire business model around exploiting one specific platform feature will face serious problems when those conditions change.
text_ko: 가끔은 페이스북 광고 플랫폼(Facebook ad platform)의 어떤 작은 뉘앙스 때문에 빠르게 확장할 수 있는 지름길(shortcuts)이나 해킹(hacks)을 찾아내기도 해요. 그런데 사람들이 못 보는 건, 그런 허점(loopholes)들은 생겼다가 금방 사라진다는 거예요.
text_zh: 有时候有人会找到一些捷径、技巧(hacks)，利用Facebook广告平台(Facebook ad platform)的某个特定细节来快速扩张。可他们没意识到的是，这些漏洞(loopholes)是暂时的，很快就会被平台堵上。
text_es: A veces la gente encuentra atajos o trucos (shortcuts, hacks), por así decirlo, para escalar muy rápido aprovechando algún matiz concreto de la plataforma de anuncios de Facebook (Facebook ad platform) o algo así. Y lo que no ven es que esos resquicios aparecen y desaparecen.
key_sentence: Hacks to scale rapidly rely on loopholes that come and go, risking business stability.
original_text: Sometimes people find shortcuts, hacks if you will, to scale rapidly because of one specific nuance of the Facebook ad platform, or something like that. And what they fail to see is that those loopholes come and go. And so if they scale massively and their entire business is predicated on the performance of this one loophole that they found, or investing everything in a single channel, and then the conditions change, they're not going to be very happy and the business will suffer dramatically.

vocabulary.definition: To grow or expand quickly in size, capacity, or number, often in response to increased demand or market opportunities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, companies often aim to scale rapidly to capture market share and maximize revenue potential before competitors can establish themselves.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase implies not just growth, but a strategic and efficient increase in operations or output.

vocabulary.definition: A subtle or slight difference in meaning, expression, or response that may not be immediately obvious.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding the nuances of market trends or consumer behavior can provide businesses with a competitive edge in tailoring their strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used to describe complexities, it can also imply the importance of paying attention to details that might otherwise be overlooked.

vocabulary.definition: Ambiguities or gaps in a system, law, or policy that can be exploited to achieve an unintended outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, loopholes in regulations or contracts can be leveraged for financial gain, but they may also pose ethical risks and potential legal repercussions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting exploitation rather than legitimate use of available options.

text: The antidote to that is to have resources dedicated to paid and essentially iterate upon the creative assets themselves based on the data that we see coming from ad sets and campaigns in various channels.
speaker: Jonathan Becker
context: Lenny asks Jonathan about the importance of creative testing in performance marketing. Jonathan explains that one major problem he sees is when brand teams create generic assets without understanding how paid channels work. He describes the solution: having dedicated resources for paid marketing that can systematically test and iterate on creative assets based on performance data, treating it as both an art and science.
text_ko: 해법은 유료 미디어(paid media)에 전담 자원을 투입해 다양한 채널의 광고 세트(ad sets)와 캠페인(campaigns)에서 나오는 데이터를 바탕으로 크리에이티브 자산(creative assets)을 계속 테스트하고 개선하는 거예요.
text_zh: 关键是要把专门的资源放到付费投放(paid)上，然后根据各渠道广告组(ad sets)和投放活动(campaigns)的数据，直接快速迭代创意素材(creative assets)。
text_es: La solución es destinar recursos a la publicidad de pago (paid) y, sobre todo, usar los datos que vienen de los conjuntos de anuncios (ad sets) y las campañas (campaigns) en los distintos canales para ir iterando y mejorando los materiales creativos (creative assets).
key_sentence: The antidote to that is to iterate upon creative assets and isolate variables effectively.
original_text: The antidote to that is to have resources dedicated to paid and essentially iterate upon the creative assets themselves based on the data that we see coming from ad sets and campaigns in various channels. And so what that means is that you have to experiment. You have to take a bit of a scientific approach, although it's a bit of an art and a bit of a science. You have to try and isolate variables, maintain similar conditions across targeting, and then determine which style and feature of an ad performs best at which stage of the funnel versus which audience.

vocabulary.definition: To perform a process or procedure repeatedly, often with the aim of improving or refining the outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, 'iterate' is commonly used in product development and project management to describe the continuous improvement of products or strategies based on feedback and testing.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'iterate' suggests a positive, constructive approach to development, it can imply a lack of finality or a need for ongoing adjustments.

vocabulary.definition: Materials or resources that are used to convey a brand's message, including graphics, videos, and written content.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and advertising, creative assets are essential for campaigns as they help to engage audiences and communicate brand identity effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of originality and innovation, emphasizing the importance of unique and appealing content.

vocabulary.definition: Facts, statistics, or information collected for analysis and reference, often used to inform decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, data is critical for understanding market trends, customer behavior, and the effectiveness of strategies, guiding companies in their strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'data' is often seen as objective and factual, it can also be interpreted subjectively depending on how it is analyzed and presented.

vocabulary.definition: Coordinated series of activities or actions designed to achieve a specific goal, often related to marketing or advocacy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing, campaigns are structured efforts to promote products or services, utilizing various channels to reach target audiences effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'campaign' suggests a strategic approach with planned phases and objectives, distinguishing it from more casual or uncoordinated marketing efforts.

text: We had plenty of projects that we worked on that flatlined during that period. And so the sense that there was a period of time where this was easy or it worked on any project is not correct in my opinion.
speaker: Jonathan Becker
context: Lenny asks whether startups can still scale almost exclusively through performance marketing, referencing successful companies from the 2010s. Jonathan provides a balanced perspective, explaining that while successful unicorns did use performance marketing, not every company that used performance marketing succeeded. He clarifies that there was never a time when performance marketing was universally easy or guaranteed to work, even during the supposed 'golden era' of the 2010s.
text_ko: 그 기간 동안 우리가 진행하던 프로젝트 중 상당수가 사실상 정체됐어요. 그래서 한동안 이게 쉬웠다거나 어떤 프로젝트에나 통했다는 인식은 제 생각에 맞지 않아요.
text_zh: 那段时间我们做的很多项目都停滞不前，根本没什么进展。所以，说那段时间事情很容易做、或者哪个项目都能成功，这种看法站不住脚。
text_es: Nos encontramos con muchos proyectos que se quedaron estancados durante ese período. Por eso, la sensación de que hubo una época en la que esto era fácil o que funcionaba con cualquier proyecto no es correcta, en mi opinión.
key_sentence: the sense that there was a period of time where this was easy or it worked on any project is not correct in my opinion.
original_text: We had plenty of projects that we worked on that flatlined during that period. And so the sense that there was a period of time where this was easy or it worked on any project is not correct in my opinion. With that said, we see companies that are spending millions of dollars a month on performance marketing channels like Google and Meta still, despite all the ups and downs that they have faced and they do so profitably.

vocabulary.definition: To remain at a constant level without growth or progress, often used to describe a situation that has stagnated.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business or project management, 'flatlined' refers to projects or initiatives that have failed to gain traction or show any measurable results over a period of time.
vocabulary.nuance: While it often implies a negative outcome, it can also suggest a need for reevaluation or a shift in strategy.

vocabulary.definition: Planned sets of interrelated tasks aimed at achieving a specific goal within a defined timeframe.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, projects are often used to implement new initiatives, develop products, or improve processes, and are typically managed through project management methodologies.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can encompass a wide range of activities, from small tasks to large-scale initiatives, making it essential to clarify the scope when discussing projects.
